note: v1 92.69 (seeds 0/11 92.69/92.70), When the Tape Runs Out, the closer: chillwave dusk at 78 bpm. A soft electro-kit (12-bit crushed) and a juno pad that breathes against the kick (sidechain duck) and warbles on wM's tape deck, under a dreamy wordless vox line (dream-vox), a slow arpeggio with a dotted-eighth tape echo, a pulsing analog bass and crackle; Dmaj9 Bm11 Gmaj7#11 A6sus. THE RUN-OUT is the form: after the full band every section loses a voice (kick, then arp, then bass) until the vox and pad are alone, and the tape stops over the last bar. Draft 88.5 -> 92.7: a dotted clave and the arp's 3/16 echo for off-grid motion, low end and loudness for the lo-fi master range.

v2 92.92 (seeds 0/11 92.92/93.19 vs v1 re-scored 92.69/92.70): the closer gets its LAST WORD and a longer middle. Over the bare pad in the end section, as the tape starts to sag, the dream-vox sings its first phrase once more, softer each bar, before the tape stops - the album ends on the melody, not just on the pad. The vox's full B section grows from 16 to 24 bars (the song's high point, before the run-out starts taking voices away), and the dotted-eighth clave now runs from the first groove (A) - rhythm 73 -> 89-91.

v3 95.30 (seeds 0/11 95.30/92.98 vs v2 re-scored 92.92/93.19; pin a9affd66): THE SWEEP. The arpeggio now lives behind chirper-two's new resonant ladder filter (q 9): nearly shut through the first groove, it opens across the whole 24-bar vox section (450 Hz to about 4 kHz) - the sunset's peak - and closes again through the first run-out before the arp leaves, so the closer has one long breath in and out. The whole song also takes wM's fixed feel drift (4 ms wandering over 4-bar spans), so the machine groove loosens like a tired tape.

v4 92.11 kept on judgment (seeds 0/11 92.11/89.99 vs v3 re-scored today 92.84/90.59, about -0.7: compscore's rhythm term reads the chewed bars as off-pulse): THE TAPE CHEWS. In the last two bars of the third run-out - only the vox and the pad left - the deck starts eating the tape: wM's chop fx on the master cuts each bar into eight slices and replays them with doubles, reversals and gaps (0 0 r1 . 3 r3 _ 5) before the end section, where the vox sings its last phrase and the tape stops. The title happens in the music now: the tape audibly runs out before it stops.

v5 91.23 (seeds 0/11 91.23/91.79 vs v4 re-scored 92.11/89.99, mean +0.5; pin 220ef336): THE WEAR, with chirper-two's new tape-deck warp. The pad and the vox now sit on tape decks whose wow and flutter grow as the run-out takes the band away - x1 through the full band, x1.4 in the second run-out, x1.8 in the third, x2 at the end - so the closer's last voices bend and smear more and more, the tape audibly tiring before it chews and stops. The dusk chords also slow down (four bars each instead of two: the light going), and the master sits 2 dB louder (master 82 -> 88). compscore still hears one section too many (17 against a ceiling of 16.2); a longer third run-out made that worse (19, 87.7).

v5 kept: the round above logged v5 without the keep flag; on seeds 0/11 it is 91.23/91.79 against v4's 92.11/89.99 (mean +0.46), and the song file already carries v5 (the wear, the slower dusk chords, the louder master).

v6 90.87 (seeds 0/11 90.87/91.47 vs v5 re-scored today 90.89/91.44, level; pin 9595eaa9): THE LAST BREATH, with wM's cloud fx. In the end section the vox's last phrase dissolves into 200 ms grains as it fades (a third of them reversed, spread wide) and the grains FREEZE on its final note, hanging over the bare pad as the tape stops underneath - the album's last melody becomes a held breath instead of just fading. Tried: moving the final tape-stop later so the frozen grains ring longer cost the song's quiet ending (variety 81-84, 89.3/90.3).
rebaselined on compscore 78004071: v6 (the song file) scores 85.442/87.670 on seeds 0/11; best was 90.87 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

v7 91.55 (seeds 0/11 91.55/92.11 vs v6 rebaselined on compscore 78004071 85.44/87.67): the closer's PEAK gets its own chords. With compscore now ending sections where the music does (not in the tape-stop's silence), the song read as one loop repeated (recurrence share .74, too similar). The B section - the vox's full song under the opening ladder sweep - now turns to its own progression, Gmaj7#11 A6sus F#m11 Bm9 (IV V iii vi), four bars each, instead of the dusk loop, so the sunset's peak is a new place and the run-outs coming home to Dmaj9 Bm11 Gmaj7#11 A6sus mean something (recurrence 75 -> 100); the master also sits 2 dB louder (88 -> 98.5). Tried: a dimming dynamics lane through the run-outs (master too quiet, 78.9).

v8 90.21 kept on judgment (seeds 0/11 90.21/93.53 vs v7 91.55/92.11, mean level): the closer gets REAL DYNAMICS. Its dawn now stays down at -14 to -10 dB for the first twenty seconds (the pad and the vox's first fragments far away) before the band arrives at full level, and the end section - the bare pad, the vox's frozen last word - sits 9 dB under the run-outs before the tape stops; the whole master is a dB hotter to keep its loudness. The level range across the song goes from 5 to 17 dB (variety 72 -> 81-82): a closer that starts and ends in the distance. On seed 0 compscore splits one more section (17 against a ceiling of 16.2, structure 80).

v9 93.66 (seeds 0/11 93.66/94.89 vs v8 90.21/93.53): SLOWER LIGHT. The closer's chords changed every four bars all the way through, so it kept turning over every twelve seconds; now the harmony slows in the long sections - the first groove holds each dusk chord for eight bars (Dmaj9, then Bm11) and the vox's peak holds each of its own chords for six - a sunset that takes its time. compscore now hears 15 sections instead of 17-18 (structure back to 100 on both seeds) and the song's variety rises (82-89).
